issue_context.title: [knx] default value for attribute state not exposed when f.e. a light is turned off
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When using the `expose` feature of the `knx` component, it appears that the `default` value for an exposed entity attribute is not updated in neither the KNX bus via a group message, nor internally in the `ExposeSensor` entity. So whenever the state of an entity is `None`, the `default` value will not be sent to KNX.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.7.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

knx

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/knx/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
knx:
  expose:
    - type: binary
      entity_id: light.home_livingroom
      address: "10/2/0"
      default: false
    - type: percentU8
      entity_id: light.home_livingroom
      attribute: brightness
      default: 0
      address: "10/3/0"
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

With the config example above, the on/off state to GA `10/2/0` is sent correctly when the light is turned off, but HA is not sending any bus message to GA `10/3/0`. So the brightness state never changes for KNX.

I suspect https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/knx/expose.py#L142 to be the cause for this issue. If the `new_value` is `None` it is returned immediately instead of first checking if the `old_value` already matches the correct value for this state.
comments: @farmio here is the ticket we talked about in the blueprint thread. And I think I also found the cause for the issue, see "Additional Information" above.

Hey there @julius2342, @farmio, @marvin-w, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`knx`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L261) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

this code certainly can not work correctly. The method `_async_set_knx_value` is checking for a `None` value and would apply the `default` value if configured, but this method is never called by `_async_entity_changed` with a `None` value.

```python
    async def _async_entity_changed(self, event: Event) -> None:
        """Handle entity change."""
        new_state = event.data.get("new_state")
        new_value = self._get_expose_value(new_state)
        if new_value is None:
            return
        old_state = event.data.get("old_state")
        old_value = self._get_expose_value(old_state)
        # don't send same value sequentially
        if new_value != old_value:
            await self._async_set_knx_value(new_value)

    async def _async_set_knx_value(self, value: StateType) -> None:
        """Set new value on xknx ExposeSensor."""
        if value is None:
            if self.expose_default is None:
                return
            value = self.expose_default
        await self.device.set(value)
```

IMO the check for `None` with the fallback to `self.expose_default` would have to be done the method `_get_expose_value()` - and not `_async_set_knx_value()`, then this code should work correctly.
